<div class="history-wrap">

<section class="history-hero">
<div class="history-hero-inner">
<div>
<div class="history-kicker">The story of SoCO</div>
<h1>From one room to a community.</h1>
<p class="history-hero-dek">
The Society of Cutaneous Oncology began as a local multidisciplinary academic meeting in Boston. An unexpected move online widened the circle, and over time the group evolved into a broader scientific community built around critical discussion, collaborative research, and shared inquiry.
</p>
<div class="history-actions">
<a href="index.qmd">About SoCO</a>
<a href="community_highlights.qmd">Community Highlights</a>
</div>
</div>
<div>
<img src="img/soco-logo-stacked-transparent.png" class="history-hero-logo" alt="Society of Cutaneous Oncology logo">
</div>
</div>
</section>

<section class="history-intro">
<h2>A history shaped by conversation</h2>
<p>
The format has changed—from an in-person conference room, to Zoom, to a multi-institutional scientific community—but the central idea has remained remarkably consistent: bring people together, examine the evidence carefully, and make the discussion useful.
</p>
</section>

<div class="history-era-strip">
<div class="history-era">
<div class="history-era-year">2019</div>
<div class="history-era-label">The local beginning</div>
</div>
<div class="history-era">
<div class="history-era-year">2020</div>
<div class="history-era-label">The move online</div>
</div>
<div class="history-era">
<div class="history-era-year">2023</div>
<div class="history-era-label">SoCO takes shape</div>
</div>
<div class="history-era">
<div class="history-era-year">2025+</div>
<div class="history-era-label">A broader community</div>
</div>
</div>

<section class="history-timeline">

<div class="history-event featured">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">April 2, 2019</div>
<h3>The first meeting</h3>
<p>
The group began as an in-person multidisciplinary academic program bringing together clinicians and investigators from Massachusetts General Hospital and Mass Eye and Ear around the management of non-melanoma skin cancers.
</p>
<p>
The opening Journal Club established the model that would continue to define the group: start with a clinically important paper, then interrogate what the evidence does—and does not—support.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">First Journal Club</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.2017.77.0941">Postoperative Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy Versus Postoperative Radiotherapy in High-Risk Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: The Randomized Phase III TROG 05.01 Trial</a>
</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">Porceddu SV et al. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2018;36:1275–1283.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

<div class="history-event">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">March 3, 2020</div>
<h3>The last in-person meeting</h3>
<p>
What had started as a recurring face-to-face academic meeting held its final in-person session just before the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted clinical, academic, and professional life worldwide.
</p>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

</section>

<section class="history-pandemic">
<div class="history-pandemic-inner">
<div class="history-pandemic-label">A turning point</div>
<h3>The interruption changed the format—and ultimately the reach.</h3>
<p>
On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization characterized COVID-19 as a pandemic. The move away from in-person meetings was initially a necessity. It soon became an opportunity: geography no longer had to define who could join the conversation.
</p>
</div>
</section>

<section class="history-timeline">

<div class="history-event featured">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">May 5, 2020</div>
<h3>The group returns—online</h3>
<p>
Two months after the final in-person meeting, the program restarted on Zoom. The virtual format made it possible to invite colleagues beyond Boston and began the transition from a local institutional meeting toward a distributed academic community.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">First online Journal Club</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.20.00201">Neoadjuvant Nivolumab for Patients With Resectable Merkel Cell Carcinoma in the CheckMate 358 Trial</a>
</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">Topalian SL et al. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2020;38:2476–2487.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

<div class="history-event">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">November 8, 2022</div>
<h3>The Journal of Cutaneous Oncology begins publishing</h3>
<p>
As the academic community grew, its scientific conversations gained a durable home. The <strong>Journal of Cutaneous Oncology (JoCO)</strong> began publishing as an open-access journal dedicated to skin cancer, evidence interpretation, scientific perspective, and thoughtful discussion.
</p>
<p>
The Journal emerged during the transition from the earlier cutaneous oncology interest group toward what would soon become the Society of Cutaneous Oncology.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">First JoCO publication</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">
<a href="https://journalofcutaneousoncology.io/perspectives/vol_1_issue_1/neoadjuvant_ici_for_resectable_cscc/">Neoadjuvant ICI for Resectable CSCC</a>
</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">Miller DM, Patel VA, Cohen JV, Garmen K, Shalhout SZ. Journal of Cutaneous Oncology. 2022;1(1). Published November 8, 2022.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

<div class="history-event featured">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">March 6, 2023</div>
<h3>The Society of Cutaneous Oncology</h3>
<p>
The expanding community was formally reintroduced as the <strong>Society of Cutaneous Oncology (SoCO)</strong>. The new name reflected what the group had become: multidisciplinary, multi-institutional, and centered on the broader field of cutaneous oncology rather than any single institution or disease.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">First Journal Club as SoCO</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2203086">Nicotinamide for Skin-Cancer Chemoprevention in Transplant Recipients</a>
</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">Allen NC et al. New England Journal of Medicine. 2023;388:804–812.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

<div class="history-event">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">March 31, 2023</div>
<h3>The first Research Forum</h3>
<p>
SoCO added a second kind of scientific conversation. Rather than beginning with a published paper, the Research Forum created a place to discuss ideas still in development—study concepts, methods, unanswered questions, and opportunities for collaboration.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">Inaugural Research Forum</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">ICARUS</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">The first Research Forum focused on the ICARUS research program and established a venue for work in progress and collaborative study development.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

<div class="history-event featured">
<div class="history-event-card">
<div class="history-date">April 10, 2025</div>
<h3>The first joint academic–industry scientific session</h3>
<p>
SoCO held its first collaborative academic–industry meeting with Bristol Myers Squibb. The format extended the same principles used in Journal Club—open scientific discussion, careful evidence interpretation, and constructive critique—to a session that included both academic and industry participants.
</p>
<div class="history-paper">
<div class="history-paper-label">Discussion focus</div>
<div class="history-paper-title">
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-24-02138">Nivolumab With or Without Ipilimumab in Patients With Recurrent or Metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Nonrandomized, Open-Label, International, Multicenter Phase I/II Study</a>
</div>
<div class="history-paper-meta">Bhatia S et al. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2025;43:1137–1147. CheckMate 358.</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="history-dot"></div>
</div>

</section>

<section class="history-chapter">
<div class="history-chapter-card">
<h2>The next chapter is being written in public.</h2>
<p>
Today, SoCO brings together Journal Club, Research Forum, collaborative scientific projects, and the Journal of Cutaneous Oncology. What began as a local meeting now has both a living scientific community and a durable publishing platform. Its structure remains intentionally lightweight: the community grows through participation, and the scientific record grows through the meetings, methods, discussions, publications, and collaborations that follow.
</p>

</div>
</div>
</section>

Historical meeting dates reflect the Society's internal program record. Publication details are linked to the original articles. COVID-19 pandemic context reflects the World Health Organization's March 11, 2020 declaration.
